To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

N mineralization rates after chemically killing managed grassland can be predicted by a combination of soil organic matter (SOM) content, the N content of roots and stubble, and the age of the grassland at destruction.

the mineralization rate after killing of grass with herbicides can be predicted by the contents of total N and total C in the soil, the N content of roots and stubble, and the age of the grassland at destruction.

the mineralization rates of grasslands that were chemically killed with a herbicide, but were undisturbed otherwise, varied from 0 to 3 g N m2 wk−1; the N content of soil, the N content of roots and stubble, the age of the grassland at destruction and the content of DOC were the best predictors of the mineralization rates; the content of DON was not a good predictor of the mineralization rate after chemically killing the grass.
